resources.string: On your computer, open Continuum and click “Pair a Phone”. Then scan the code it shows.
This phone will stop connecting to it. You can pair again at any time.
Only continue if this code is shown by Continuum on your own computer, right now.
This replaces %1$s. Your phone will stop connecting to it.
It isn\'t a valid Continuum pairing code. Click “Pair a Phone” on your computer to get a new one.
Continuum needs the camera to scan the pairing code on your computer. Nothing is recorded or saved.
Point the camera at the code on your computer
That isn\'t a Continuum code. Click “Pair a Phone” on your computer.
The “Connected to your computer” notification. Turning it off doesn’t stop the connection or your other notifications.
Android still shows a small line while Continuum runs. To remove it, switch off “Connection status (hidden)” in Android settings. Continuum stays connected.
Hidden everywhere. Continuum stays connected in the background.
Waiting for Wi-Fi. It reconnects by itself when you\'re back on the same network.
Continuum needs this to find and talk to your computer on your Wi-Fi. Nothing leaves your home network. Scan the code again and tap Allow.
Continuum isn\'t allowed to use your local network. Open Settings › Apps › Continuum › Permissions and allow “Nearby devices”.
Pair Continuum with your computer first.
The app you shared from didn\'t allow Continuum to read these files.
Only files can be sent for now.
Copy on one device, paste on the other.
Nothing to send. Copy some text or an image first.
Continuum: send copies to your computer
Whatever you copy on this phone appears on your computer\'s clipboard.

Android lets only the app on screen read the clipboard. With this on, Continuum notices when you copy (a tap on “Copy” or the “Copied” message), reads the clipboard for a split second, and sends it to your paired computer over your Wi-Fi. It doesn\'t read or store anything on your screen, and nothing leaves your home network.
Copy on phone, paste on computer

Everything you copy on this phone appears on your computer, no buttons. Set it up once:\n1. Tap Turn on.\n2. Open “Downloaded apps” (or “Installed apps”), tap “Continuum: send copies to your computer” and switch it on.

3. Switch greyed out? Android does this for apps not from the Play Store. Tap App info below › ⋮ (top right) › “Allow restricted settings”, then repeat step 2.\nTip: Android then says “Continuum pasted from your clipboard” after each copy. To hide that, search Settings for “clipboard” and turn off “Show clipboard access”.
Android needs your OK once: switch on “Allow from this source” for Continuum, then come back and tap Update.
Copy new screenshots to the computer
Take a screenshot here, then press Ctrl+V on the computer. Needs Gallery access.
See your photos and videos on the computer
Read and send texts from the computer
See phone notifications on the computer
Browse phone storage from the computer

See all your phone's photos and videos on the computer, newest first.

• On the computer, open Continuum and choose Gallery.
• Open a photo to see it full size, or copy it and paste it anywhere.
• Save photos and videos to the computer in one click.

Photos are read only when the computer asks for them, over your encrypted connection. Nothing is uploaded to the internet.

Browse your phone's storage from the computer, like a USB drive but over Wi-Fi.

• On the computer, choose Phone Storage.
• Open folders and download any file to the computer.
• To send files the other way, use Send Files.

Android calls this permission “All files access”. Continuum uses it only while you browse from your paired computer.

Read and reply to your text messages (SMS) from the computer.

• On the computer, choose Messages to see your conversations.
• Type a reply there; your phone sends it as a normal text.

Messages go only between your phone and your paired computer. They are never stored on a server.

See your phone's notifications on the computer as they arrive.

• Reply to chats right from the notification, where the app allows it.
• Use the notification's buttons, or dismiss it on the computer and it goes from the phone too.

Android calls this permission “Notification access”. Notifications go only to your paired computer.
Partly allowed: only the photos you picked
Android won\'t ask again. Tap App info › Permissions and allow it there.
Blocked? Tap App info › ⋮ (top right) › “Allow restricted settings”, then Permissions › SMS.
Switch greyed out? Tap App info › ⋮ (top right) › “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.
Continuum: show notifications on your computer
Your computer is looking for this phone.
A progress bar while files go to or come from your computer.
When files from your computer have arrived. Tap one to open it.
When files from this phone have reached your computer.
When files couldn\'t be sent or received.
“Connected to your computer” while Continuum runs.
A small, silent version of the connection notification. Switch it off to hide it completely.
When a new version of Continuum is ready.
Rings this phone when you look for it from your computer.
Everything you copy here shows up on your computer. Takes a minute to set up.
Allow Continuum to run when the app is closed, so your phone and computer stay connected.
Xiaomi phones close background apps. Allow background running and turn on “Autostart” for Continuum.
Xiaomi phones need this on to reconnect after a restart.
On. What you copy here appears on your computer.
Choose which notifications you get. Each one opens Android\'s settings for it.
You won\'t see any of the ones below. Tap to turn them on.
A new version is ready. See below.
Couldn\'t reach GitHub. Check your internet and try again.
This is a development build. It doesn\'t update itself.
Free and open source (GPL-3.0) on GitHub
Downloaded and checked. Tap Install, then confirm on the next screen.
Asks before your screen is shown on the computer, and shows while it is
Everything on your screen is visible there
Can\'t reach your computer. Make sure Continuum is running there and both are on the same Wi-Fi.
Use this phone from your computer while its screen is mirrored there

Lets your paired computer tap, swipe, scroll and type on this phone, but only while you are mirroring its screen to it (you tap “Start now” on the phone first, and Android shows that it’s being shared). Continuum reads the text field you type into, nothing else, and sends nothing from this service anywhere.
Xiaomi phones: allow “Open new windows while running in the background” (on some versions “Display pop-up windows…”), so the phone asks to share its screen by itself
On: the computer’s mouse and keyboard work while mirroring. Tap to turn it off.
Off: the computer only shows your screen
Click Mirror in Continuum on the computer. The first time, the phone asks you to allow screen sharing. No developer options or USB debugging needed.

1. Tap Turn on, find “Continuum remote control” (on some phones under Downloaded apps or Installed services) and switch it on. 2. The computer can then use the phone only while its screen is mirrored.
Switch greyed out? Android does this for apps not from the Play Store. Tap App info › ⋮ (top right) › “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.
On: developer options, USB debugging and Continuum’s helpers are off, so banking apps open
Off: developer options are on (banking apps may refuse to open)
One tap to switch developer options and USB debugging off for banking apps, and back on
Tip: add the Banking mode tile to Quick Settings (pull down twice › edit ✎). If a banking app was already open, close and reopen it.
Switch banking mode from the notification shade with one tap

Android lets an app switch developer options only after a one-time permission from a computer: 1. Keep USB debugging on and connect the phone to the computer with a USB cable. 2. On the computer, run the command below (from Android platform tools). 3. Come back here: the switch appears. It keeps working after you turn USB debugging off. On Xiaomi phones, also turn on “USB debugging (Security settings)” in developer options before step 2.
Banking mode on: developer options, USB debugging and Continuum’s helpers are off. Reopen your banking app.
Banking mode off: developer options, USB debugging and Continuum’s helpers are back on.
